newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends flat, RBI, SBI buy dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends flat, RBI, SBI buy dollars.

text.p: The rupee closed nearly unchanged at 35.765/775 on Tuesday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the State Bank of India (SBI) stepped in to buy dollars towards the close of trading, dealers said.
The rupee had opened the day flat at 35.76/77 per dollar and moved in a 35.760-35.7750 range, they said.
The RBI intervened in the last hour of trading, buying dollars at 35.77, dealers said. RBI was not an aggressive buyer and one dealer described its intervention as "token."
"SBI came minutes before the market closed and bought upto 35.775 level," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
Many dealers were hoping for signs of month-end spurt in dollar demand, but is is unclear whether SBI's dollar demand would continue for the next few days, they said.
Even if SBI's dollar buying continued, the rupee was unlikely to breach 35.78 mark, dealers said.
But for dollar purchases by these two dominant players, the market was extremely dull throughout the day, dealers said.
"It is as if the market was on a strike," a dealer at a foreign bank said on Tuesday afternoon.
The forward dollar market continued to be stuck at earlier low levels. The six-month annualised premium closed at 4.36 percent on Wednesday compared with the previous 4.42 percent.

"Forwards remain stuck for three days in a row," said a dealer. "Some paying by institutions and fear of RBI buying forward dollars is holding the premiums up in the face of easy liquidity and far-end exporter covering," he said.
